flags.title: Market status words differ between the filter and the response
flags.detail: The GET /markets status filter uses unopened / open / paused / closed / settled, but the Market.status field in responses uses initialized / inactive / active / closed / determined / disputed / amended / finalized. The dashboard treats status 'active' as tradable (the response value). Confirm this mapping with Kalshi before relying on status filters.

flags.title: Fee rounding wording vs. the fee table
flags.detail: The fee schedule says 'round up such that the fee + positionCost is rounded to a centicent', but every table value is a whole-cent amount. The code rounds the fee up to the whole cent. All 21 General Trading Fees Table rows (1-contract and 100-contract columns) match, and the test passes. Ask Kalshi to confirm the rounding rule for fractional-cent positions.

flags.title: Fee schedule PDF text layer is scrambled in parts
flags.detail: The Non-Standard Fees table (MLB, NCAA, NFL, NBA and other series pages) is garbled in the extracted text (for example overlapping titles such as 'WRoeoskteiernof'). The dashboard does not hard-code those multipliers. It reads fee_type and fee_multiplier for each series from the live API. A human should open the PDF and compare any series used for trading.

flags.title: SDK package metadata has placeholders
flags.detail: The kalshi-typescript npm metadata lists repository and homepage as https://github.com/GIT_USER_ID/GIT_REPO_ID, which are unfilled template placeholders. The package is published by a maintainer named 'kalshi' (npm metadata), so the publisher is plausibly Kalshi, but the source repository could not be confirmed from the package metadata.

flags.title: SDK default base URL is production, not demo
flags.detail: The official SDK's default BASE_PATH is https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2 (production). Code copied from SDK examples without a base override calls production, while the project brief names demo hosts. Keys are environment-specific (S3, S6).

flags.title: Rate limit for unauthenticated public requests is not stated
flags.detail: The rate-limit page says unauthenticated requests have separate limits and to back off on 429, but gives no number. The collector limits itself to about 7 requests per second, retries on 429/5xx with backoff, and runs about every 30 minutes. Its real headroom is unverified.

flags.title: Prior snapshot may contain production data until demo refresh succeeds
flags.detail: The secondary collector previously defaulted to production, contrary to the demo-only project scope. The collector now defaults to Kalshi's official demo REST root and rejects production/custom hosts before making requests. This flag remains open until a successful new demo collection replaces the older production snapshot; inspect source.base_url and generated_at in the published data.

flags.title: Demo-account portfolio and trade execution are NOT connected
flags.detail: Reading the demo account and placing demo orders need a demo API key pair created in Kalshi account settings. Those keys were not provided and cannot be created from this session, so no live balance or positions are shown and no orders have been placed. Two pieces that used to be missing are now in place, so this flag is only about the credential: dashboard.yml runs the read-only snapshot step when the secrets exist (add repository secrets KALSHI_DEMO_KEY_ID and KALSHI_DEMO_PRIVATE_KEY), and the trades page now renders kalshi-dashboard/data/portfolio.json when it exists and states which of the three states applies (no file / file says not connected / connected). The signing code follows the official spec (S6) and is tested offline. Until the credential exists, the published snapshot file will not appear and the page says so.

flags.title: Second-level price TICKS need a streaming server; the alerts feed no longer waits for a collector run
flags.detail: Two limits, now separated. (a) Alerts: since 2026-11-21 the alerts page also measures in the visitor's browser — one anonymous GET /markets/orderbooks per 45 s for up to 100 markets, same >= $0.10 rule and same quote-integrity refusals as the collector — so the chats do not go quiet between scheduled runs. (b) Charts: still limited to collector samples, because the price graph plots the collector's history and Kalshi's own candlestick periods are 1 minute, 1 hour and 1 day. A sub-minute axis therefore needs either the browser poll to be recorded as history (not built) or a small always-on service holding an API key and streaming WebSocket ticks; GitHub Pages is static and the WebSocket handshake needs KALSHI-ACCESS-* headers a browser cannot set (S8).

flags.title: 'Est. 24h $ volume' is a derived estimate, not an official Kalshi dollar figure

flags.title: 'High-ROI' is a placeholder rule, not your model
flags.detail: No model was provided. The dashboard uses a transparent rule (entry ≤ 40¢, spread ≤ 5¢, 24h volume ≥ 100 contracts) defined in config/topics.json. Replace it with your model's outputs when available. The rule is not a prediction and makes no claim about profitability.

flags.title: Resolution coverage is bounded by design: a rotating settled scan, not an exhaustive history
flags.detail: What the settled scan can and cannot see, stated so a reader can judge a gap. (1) GET /markets accepts ONE status at a time and the sweep is bounded: RESOLUTION_SCAN_MAX_SERIES series per run, rotated on a 15-minute window, and a hard RESOLUTION_SCAN_MAX_REQUESTS page budget, so a busy series is read page by page across several runs rather than all at once; the run record publishes settled_scan_series / _markets / _requests / _pages / _duplicates_deduped / _budget so truncation is visible. (2) Lookback is 30 days (min_settled_ts); Kalshi documents that markets settled before its historical cutoff are only available through GET /historical/markets, so older resolutions are out of scope. (3) The docs warn that filtered listings can lag behind the market endpoint, so a settlement may appear on the next run rather than the current one. (4) A market the collector never saw open has no event title: the row publishes market_title and leaves event_title null - never a relabelled market title. (5) result values other than yes/no (scalar, empty) are not published as outcomes. (6) No row carries a news or website cause link: no API field provides one (F-10). The prior defect - resolved.json permanently empty because only the top-80 tracked tickers were re-read - is what this scan replaced (Board M8A8, 2026-11-21).

flags.title: GET /portfolio/balance does not state a unit for its integer `balance` and `portfolio_value` fields
flags.detail: The documented response is {"balance": 123, "balance_dollars": "0.5600", "portfolio_value": 123, "updated_ts": 123, "balance_breakdown": [{"exchange_index": 0, "balance": "0.5600"}]}. `balance_dollars` and the breakdown's `balance` are dollar strings, while the top-level `balance` and `portfolio_value` are bare integers with no unit on this page, and `updated_ts` is a bare number while positions carry an ISO `last_updated_ts`. The example values are placeholders and are not self-consistent (123 vs 0.5600). scripts/portfolio.mjs therefore publishes them unconverted and the trades page prints them as returned, labelled as such; nothing on the site divides them by 100 or calls them cents. Also unverified: whether `updated_ts` is seconds or milliseconds — shown raw. This stays open until a real demo key pair lets a live snapshot be compared against the account screen.
